note: Machine-readable index of every data source CostAnswer uses, evaluates or has rejected. Licence fields are read from the source's own LICENSE/terms, never inferred from a repository name or from memory. A source may not enter production unless commercialUse is 'permitted'. `tier` says what role a figure from this source plays in an answer, which is what decides the word printed beside it on a calculation receipt; `lib/data/data-sources.ts` is the code that reads it and the two are asserted to agree. A row with `partOf` is one document inside a compiled source: the tax snapshot is transcribed from several IRS publications and 51 state revenue departments, and ships as one source called `us-tax`.

trustLevels.primary: The body that creates the number. Its own publication is the authority.
trustLevels.secondary: Republishes or compiles primary figures. Usable to find and cross-check, never as the final value.
trustLevels.discovery: Not a data source. Used to locate the primary document, or to learn structure.
trustLevels.rejected: Evaluated and excluded. The reason is recorded so it is not re-evaluated.

sources.name: City of Austin Issued Construction Permits
sources.attribution: Source: City of Austin open data
limitations: Trade permits carry no valuation. Of residential permits issued since 2023, mechanical, electrical and plumbing permits populate their valuation columns in single-digit counts against tens of thousands of rows, so HVAC, water-heater and panel jobs cannot be observed here at all.

Valuation is per permit, not per scope. A permit whose description mentions a deck averages $226,000 because the deck is part of a whole-house remodel; keyword matching therefore attributes an entire job to one line item.

A strict filter does work for a few scopes — 109 Austin permits since 2023 are window replacement and nothing else, median $10,350 — but that is one metro, a few jobs, and a valuation declared before the work rather than an invoice after it.

sources.name: Los Angeles building permits issued
sources.licenseVerifiedFrom: Socrata dataset metadata, license field is null, 2026-09-08
sources.attribution: Source: City of Los Angeles open data
limitations: The portal states no licence on this dataset, so commercial use is not cleared and it may not enter production under this project’s own rule.
It carries building permits only — no separate mechanical, electrical or plumbing permits — so it has the same blind spot as Austin for equipment-replacement jobs.

sources.name: USACE Construction Equipment Ownership and Operating Expense Schedule (EP 1110-1-8)
sources.attribution: Source: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
limitations: The publications host answers automated requests with HTTP 403, and the schedule ships as regional PDFs rather than a machine-readable table, so ingesting it is a transcription project rather than a fetch.
It is richer than the FEMA schedule already in use — it carries regional and age factors FEMA does not — which is why it stays a named candidate rather than being dropped.

sources.name: Census Economic Census, Administrative and Support Services (sector 56)
sources.attribution: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2022 Economic Census
limitations: The sector 56 basic file reports revenue, payroll and employment only. Without cost of materials, construction-worker hours and fringe benefits the direct/overhead/profit split computed for construction cannot be reproduced, so tree removal keeps its modelled business rates rather than borrowing a construction trade’s.

sources.name: buildstock-fetch
sources.attribution: n/a
limitations: A downloader for ResStock and ComStock outputs, not a dataset. Scanning it for prices finds nothing because there are none in it; the data it fetches lives on OEDI.

sources.name: OpenTakeoff, qto and similar quantity-takeoff projects
sources.attribution: n/a
limitations: Quantity-takeoff software. They measure drawings; they carry no unit prices, so they cannot answer what a job costs.

tiers.A: Calculation source of truth. The publisher sets the number or the rule and we reproduce it. Printed as VERIFIED.
tiers.B: Official observed data. The publisher measures something and we use the measurement. Printed as OBSERVED.
tiers.C: Model calibration. Real observations that cannot be quoted as a price on their own. Printed as MODELED.
tiers.D: CostAnswer model. A value we chose and review. Printed as MODELED.
tiers.none: Not shipped: a discovery aid, an evaluated candidate, or a rejected source.
